Publisher: Parisiis: excudebatur et venit apud J.-P. Migne editorem (title page)
Publication Date: 1853 (title page)
Rights: Public Domain (pd-us-by-date: published 1853); the archive.org record carries no rights field, so the imprint date is the basis
Language: lat
Source: archive.org item bim_early-english-books-1641-1700_1853_151, full text from the item's own djvu.txt. Fetched directly 2026-11-15 by the Library thread; the byte count of the downloaded file (4,194,323) equals the size archive.org lists for the djvu.txt.
Provenance note: Extracted unaltered: the item's own djvu.txt is reproduced whole after this header; nothing was stripped, normalized or corrected. Rights basis: published 1853, out of US copyright by date. OCR quality: the Latin is fair to poor: letters are misread and capitals stray, though most words can be made out. Line numbers cited in this header are lines of the host OCR; add 12 for this file's own line numbers.
Content note: Urban II's Life with Ruinart's notes, including the Council of Clermont, at about OCR lines 12200-15100 (the council at 13622-15012). His letters and privileges from about 22757. The speeches at Clermont, 'Orationes in concilio Claromontano habitae', in several versions, from about 46652 to about 47750. No separate text of the Clermont canons is printed.

nee non et ea qua injuste ab aliquibus possidentur, 
aut in urbe Roma, vel in cœteris totius regni nostri 
lialici partibus habere dignoscitur, per hoc nostrum 
præceptum eidem santo loco conſirmamus, et per

largienda sunt monasterio, cum omnibus suis per- 
linentiis. De teloneis vero mercatorum, et pontium, 
decimas ad portam monasterii dare jubemus. Fræ- 
cipientes ergo jubemus ut nullus archiepiscopus,

aliquis missus noster discurrens, sculdasius, castal-

seu aliquem ſidelem inquietare, molestare, aut, de his 
quæ suprascripta sunt, sine legali judicio disvestire 
præsumat, aut aliquam minorationem ſacere tentet. 

Unde monemus fidelitatem vestram, ut cum jam 
ſatus abbas, vel monachi, aut advocatus ejusder1 
monasterii in vestra ministeria justitias requirendss 
venerit, duces, seu comiles, qui pro tempore ſuc- 
rint, in quorum ducatu vel comitatu præſatum cœ- 
nobium aliquid possidere dignoscitur, deſensores, 
atque adjutores existant in omnibus, tam prifato 
abbati quam successoribus ejus, ut nullius potestatis

rouge. Quoiqu'il ſaille assurèment pardonner beaucoup à Vignorance des auteurs et à la grossierele des

Gall, de Morbach et de Reichnau (186).
